chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Umar ibn Aban al-Kalbi, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There are four thousand angels by the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), dishevelled and dusty, weeping for him until the Day of Resurrection. Their chief is an angel called Mansour. So no visitor visits him but they welcome him, and no one bids him farewell but they accompany him; and no sick person becomes ill but they visit him, and no deceased person dies but they pray over his funeral and seek forgiveness for him after his death.'

key_terms.شُعْثٍ غُبْرٍ: Dishevelled and dusty (describing the state of the angels)

ai.seo_question: What is the role of the angels at the grave of Imam Al-Husayn (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi emphasizes the cosmic significance of Karbala by depicting four thousand angels, led by the chief angel Mansur, eternally weeping at Imam Al-Husayn’s (as) grave. It establishes a spiritual protocol where these celestial beings actively participate in the lifecycle of every pilgrim—welcoming visitors, accompanying the departing, visiting the sick, and praying for the deceased—thereby linking the physical act of Ziyarah to continuous divine intercession.
